number.why: The counts 25/400 versus 47/395 are correct for day-28 mortality, but do not establish the served 30-day or in-hospital outcome. No supplied evidence establishes that day 28 is within an accepted window. The source reports 795 analyzed out of 800 randomized without establishing an intention-to-treat analysis. The served RR is reconstructable from the counts, but the published between-arm estimate and 95% CI are an absolute difference, not an RR.

quotes.span: By day 28, death had occurred in 25 of 400 patients (6.2%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 3.9 to 8.6) in the hydrocortisone group and in 47 of 395 patients (11.9%; 95% CI, 8.7 to 15.1) in the placebo group (absolute difference, -5.6 percentage points; 95% CI, -9.6 to -1.7; P = 0.006).
A total of 800 patients had undergone randomization when the trial was stopped after the second planned interim analysis. Data from 795 patients were analyzed.
PROTOCOL PRIMARY OUTCOME: Day 28 all causes mortality |  | TIME FRAME: at day 28

entry.why: Adults admitted to an ICU for severe community-acquired pneumonia satisfy the question's hospitalized adult population. Intravenous hydrocortisone versus placebo, both with standard therapy, also matches the question. Unverified ITT status concerns the analysis set rather than entry eligibility.

quotes.span: we assigned adults who had been admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) for severe community-acquired pneumonia to receive intravenous hydrocortisone (200 mg daily for either 4 or 7 days as determined by clinical improvement, followed by tapering for a total of 8 or 14 days) or to receive placebo. All the patients received standard therapy, including antibiotics and supportive care.

missed: The served row's 14-day follow-up confuses treatment duration with outcome timing. The source states "followed by tapering for a total of 8 or 14 days" and "The primary outcome was death at 28 days." (ref: cache/corticosteroids-cap-mortality/records.json#/records/7). This requires correction alongside the unsupported confirmation of the served timepoint.
